reason: Every geometry number reproduces exactly and the finding still dies - on two factual errors, on an overstated harm, and on a fix that misses half the surface it names and regresses the half it reaches. VERIFIED: driving master.html at 768/900/1000/1023/1024/1080/1152/1179/1180/1279/1280/1440/1920 on paper and ink, .b-plan .b-title is 452/544/544/544px through 1023 and 298px at 1024 on owner-flight, 306px on desk, climbing to a 534px (owner) / 542px (desk) cap. 22.67em -> 12.42em at one pixel is real, and the cap never regains the 544. FACTUAL ERROR 1: 'same trim' on desk is false. b.css:264 sets [data-state="desk"] .b-title { -webkit-line-clamp: none; overflow: visible } - the desk title CANNOT trim. Injecting the finding's own 62-char string on desk at 1024/1080/1152, paper and ink: it sets in FULL every time, three lines, zero ellipsis. Not one character is deleted on desk at any width. FACTUAL ERROR 2: the shipped fixture's break is not a band, it is a sliver. Stepping width by 1px, 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' returns to ONE line at 1033 on owner-flight (paper and ink) and at 1025 on desk (paper and ink). The two-line break the finding leads with exists across 9px of owner width and 1px of desk width, not across 1024-1279; the finding cites 1023 and 1152 as one-liners and omits that 1033 is one too. HARM OVERSTATED: the deletion demo needs a 62-char title - 2.3x the longest of the ten shipped titles (max 27 chars, 'Menu tasting at The Orchard') - and that same string is trimmed at 390 by the same designed mechanism, with the full text kept in data-full, the title attribute and a .tl-vh twin (render-core.js clamp/unhide). Screenshotted at 1024x768, the unpatched result is a balanced two-line 24px title under a 148px numeral: a wrap, not a wound. THE FIX DOES NOT REACH DESK. .b-plan exists only on the owner states; measured, the desk title's ancestor chain is .b-copy > .b-item > .b-measure > div > .b-two - no .b-plan node at all. Applying the proposed CSS verbatim and re-measuring: owner-flight goes 24px->17px across 1024-1179 as claimed, desk stays at 24px/306px/12.75em at 1024 and 12.75->19.21em across the whole band. The finding names desk as an affected surface, measures it at 306px, and then leaves it exactly where it found it; 'verified on both grounds' verified paper vs ink, not owner vs desk. THE FIX REGRESSES WHERE IT DOES REACH. (a) It trades one measure discontinuity for two size discontinuities in the reading tier: 24->17px at 1023->1024 and 17->24px at 1179->1180. A 29% size drop of 'the largest reading-tier object on the plan' at one pixel of window growth is the exact harm the finding's own headline condemns, and it now happens twice. (b) It makes the ramp non-monotonic against window width - 17 at 390, 24 at 701-1023, 17 at 1024-1179, 24 at 1180+ - contradicting the responsive type policy this panel has already settled twice (type-frozen-across-the-391-766-band and unit-never-grows-with-its-numeral: four objects step once, at 701, and the display/reading tier grades with the STAGE). This fix grades it with a pane instead. (c) Measured, .b-num (148px) and .b-when (30px) live in .b-stick and the patch does not touch them, so at 1024-1179 the owner's own words drop to 17px beside an untouched 148px numeral - straight against the defect library's 'A person's words outrank the machine's'. Screenshotted base vs patched at 1024 and 1152: the patched plan reads as a caption list, the base reads as the plan. (d) It costs a size step across 147 of its own 156px for nothing. At 1152 the base title box is 426px holding ~305px of text on one line - 120px of unused slack; the measure is not binding anywhere from 1033 to 1179, and the patch shrinks the title there anyway. (e) It buys ~20 characters of trim headroom (2x298/24 ~ 50 chars -> 2x298/17 ~ 70 chars); a 90-char title still trims. It moves a threshold, it does not remove the class. Finally, 45%-at-one-pixel is what a breakpoint IS: any boundary at X makes the post-X layout tightest at exactly X. Round 7 adjudicated that trade on measured evidence - the first moment moving from y=941 to y=570 and 371px of height - and the '534 never regains 544' clincher is a 1.8% difference. Severity '3' on a scale whose largest finding is 1.0 is not defensible for a 9px wrap window and a fix that leaves the desk untouched.
sharpenedFix: Nothing to apply. If the founder ever wants the 1024 pane wider it is a build, not two declarations: the only honest levers are the 344px rail (ratified, gate-measured) or the boundary itself (round 7's, and moving it back re-opens the confirmed height defect). A pane-scoped type step is the wrong lever - it must at minimum be scoped to .b-two's second column so desk is included, and even then it introduces a second reading-tier breakpoint into a ramp the panel has twice settled as stepping once at 701.
